              REPLY BRIEF OF OLD DOMINION ELECTRIC COOPERATIVE

          Pursuant to the Order issued in the above-referenced proceeding on December 18, 2025, 1

and the Notice of Extension of Time issued on January 23, 2026, Old Dominion Electric

Cooperative (“ODEC”) submits this Reply Brief in response to the Initial Brief and Joint

Responses of the PJM Transmission Owners to Paper Hearing Questions 2 and the Initial Brief of

PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”).

     I.   RELEVANT BACKGROUND AND SUMMARY OF POSITION

          The detailed background of this proceeding is contained in the Hearing Order. In summary,

the Commission determined that PJM’s Tariff is unjust and unreasonable because it lacked

provisions that address with sufficient clarity or consistency the rates, terms and conditions of

service that apply to generators serving Co-Located Load and Eligible Customers taking

transmission service on behalf of Co-Located Load.3 Among other things, the Commission


1
  PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 193 FERC ¶ 61,217 (2025) (“Hearing Order”).
2
  (“Indicated TOs’ Initial Brief”).
3
  Hearing Order at P 2.

                                                  2
 directed PJM to submit a compliance filing to revise its Tariff to set forth conditions for

interconnection regarding Co-Located Location Arrangements. The Commission also directed

PJM to revise its Tariff to require Eligible Customers taking transmission service on behalf of Co-

Located Loads to take one of three transmission services: (1) Network Integration Transmission

Service (“NITS”); (2) a new Firm Contract Demand transmission service; or (3) a new Non-Firm

Contract Demand transmission service.4 The Commission established a paper hearing to determine

the just and reasonable rates, terms and conditions for the new transmission services.5

          On February 23, 2026, PJM and the Indicated PJM TOs each filed their initial briefs in this

paper hearing proceeding. PJM’s Initial Brief addressed the non-rate terms and conditions for the

new transmission services, in response to questions posed in the Hearing Order. The Indicated TOs

submitted rates for the new services, consistent with their rights under the Consolidated

Transmission Owners Agreement.

          ODEC is a not-for-profit power supply electric cooperative, organized and operating under

the laws of Virginia and subject to FERC jurisdiction. ODEC supplies capacity and energy to its

eleven electric distribution cooperative members, all of which are located within the PJM control

area. ODEC is a network transmission customer of PJM, as well as a PJM Transmission Owner.

ODEC is a generation-owning utility, dependent upon the use of the transmission facilities of PJM

under its Tariff to deliver the output of ODEC’s generation facilities located within PJM and to

deliver periodic power purchases from third party sellers to the load of its member systems in

PJM’s footprint. ODEC takes transmission service under the PJM Tariff. ODEC is also a Market

Seller of energy and capacity under the PJM Tariff.

        As discussed herein, ODEC generally agrees with the proposals submitted by PJM and the

Indicated TOs in their respective Initial Briefs. Subject to the clarifications discussed below,

ODEC believes that both Initial Briefs provide just and reasonable rates, terms and conditions for

the new Firm Contract Demand transmission service and Non-Firm Contract Demand transmission

service. ODEC is willing to adopt the Indicated TOs’ proposed rates for the new Firm Contract

Demand and Non-Firm Contract Demand, subject to these clarifications. Therefore, ODEC

supports the Commission’s acceptance of both filings, subject to further compliance filings as

necessary to address the following issues described in the remainder of this Reply Brief: (1)

clarification of PJM’s proposed requirement that an Eligible Customer must be designated to take

transmission service on behalf of a Co-Located Load and provide PJM with an authorization from

its Relevant Electric Retail Regulatory Authority (“RERRA”); (2) with respect to the PJM TOs’

proposal for PJM to provide billing credits to reflect revenues associated with the new Grid

Reliance Charge as well as revenues for Non-Firm Contract Demand Service, the individual TOs

will need to either confirm that their formula or stated rates and metrics reporting enable the direct

crediting by PJM, or provide whatever revisions are necessary in order for PJM to do so; (3) PJM

and the PJM Transmission Owners will need to address how to charge regulation and black start

service to an Eligible Customer taking service on behalf of Co-Located Load; and (4) the

Commission should consider whether any protections are needed for local utilities or TOs should

they need to take the extraordinary measure of disconnecting an Eligible Customer taking service

on behalf of Co-Located Loads, if the Eligible Customer’s use of the transmission system exceeds

contract demand or they are called upon for Load Shedding and Curtailment.




                                                  4
     II.    REPLY TO PJM AND INDICATED TOS’ INITIAL BRIEFS

           ODEC is a PJM Transmission Owner but did not participate in the Indicated TOs’ Initial

Brief. ODEC submits this Reply Brief to state its support for most of the proposals in the Indicated

TOs’ Initial Brief, as well as identify areas that require further consideration or clarification.

Subject to the clarifications and issues raised below, ODEC is willing to adopt the Indicated TOs’

proposed rates for the new transmission services for Co-Located Loads, as described in the

Indicated TOs’ Initial Brief.

           Overall, ODEC agrees with the Indicated TOs’ Initial Brief and PJM’s Initial Brief.

Without detailing each component of the Indicated TOs’ Initial Brief, ODEC agrees with the

Indicated TOs’ principles that (1) rates for the new services ordered by the Commission must be

consistent with longstanding cost allocation principles, so that existing customers do not unfairly

subsidize services for Co-Located Load customers; and (2) the new transmission services must be

implemented in a manner that does not compromise system reliability.6 ODEC’s comments below

correspond to the questions posed in the Commission’s Hearing Order.

           Questions 1 and 2:

           (1) What are the appropriate rates, terms, and conditions for the new Firm Contract
               Demand transmission service, including whether it would be just and reasonable
               to apply the current zonal firm PTPS charges to this new service and whether it
               would be just and reasonable and consistent with cost causation to include charges
               for any of PJM’s administrative services?

           (2) What are the appropriate rates, terms, and conditions for the new Non-Firm
               Contract Demand transmission service, including whether it would be just and
               reasonable to apply the current zonal non-firm PTPS charges to this new
               transmission service and whether it would be just and reasonable and consistent
               with cost causation to include charges for any of PJM’s administrative services?




6
    Indicated TOs’ Initial Brief at 3-5.

                                                 5
            A. PJM’s Proposed Conditions Precedent and Technical Requirements for Contract

               Demand Transmission Services

           ODEC generally supports PJM’s conditions precedent to ensure that Eligible Customers

taking service on behalf of Co-Located Loads preserve the reliability of the Transmission System.

However, there is one aspect of PJM’s proposed conditions precedent that may need further

consideration or clarification. PJM’s Initial Brief and Illustrative Tariff propose a condition

precedent that the “Eligible Customer must have been designated to take transmission service on

behalf of a Co-Located Load in the relevant Application, Service Agreement, or GIA for the Co-

Located Generating Facility, and provide PJM with ‘an authorization or certification from its

Relevant Electric Retail Regulatory Authority which affirms that the Eligible Customer is

authorized to provide energy to the Co-Located Load.”7 Based on the existing PJM Tariff

definitions, it appears that ODEC would be the Eligible Customer8 for at least its distribution

cooperative members, as well as the RERRA.

           The PJM Tariff defines and Eligible Customer as follows:

            . . .any electric utility or any person generating electric energy for sale for resale,
           but with respect to transmission service that the Commission is prohibited from
           ordering by section 212(h) of the Federal Power Act, such entity is eligible only if
           the service is provided pursuant to a state requirement that the Transmission
           Provider or Transmission Owner offer the unbundled transmission service, or
           pursuant to a voluntary offer of such service by a Transmission Owner or (2) any
           retail customer taking unbundled transmission service pursuant to a state
           requirement that the Transmission Provider or a Transmission Owner offer the
           transmission service, or pursuant to a voluntary offer of such service by a
           Transmission Owner.

           ODEC is a generation and transmission electric cooperative. To meet the requirements of

its eleven distribution cooperatives under the Third Amended and Restated Wholesale Power


7
    PJM Initial Brief at 19; Illustrative Tariff. Part XI, Subpart B, section 710.1.
8
    PJM, Intra-PJM Tariffs, OATT, § I.1 Definitions – E-F (41.0.0).


                                                         6
 Contracts between ODEC and each of its eleven distribution electric cooperatives, ODEC owns

generating facilities and purchases Network Integration Transmission Service (“NITS”) under the

PJM Open Access Transmission Tariff (“Tariff”). Thus, with respect to the definition of Eligible

Customer, ODEC is the “electric utility . . . generating electric energy for resale” and ODEC takes

transmission service to serve its members. As such, ODEC is the entity that would be the Eligible

Customer for Co-Located Loads, at least with respect to existing generating facilities and any

Planned Facilities owned by ODEC that would be used to serve the Co-Located Loads of ODEC’s

members.

          The PJM Tariff defines the RERRA as “an entity that has jurisdiction over and establishes

prices and policies for competition for providers of retail electric service to end-customers, such

as the city council for a municipal utility, the governing board of a cooperative utility, the state

public utility commission or any other such entity.”9 ODEC’s members are located in Virginia,

Maryland and Delaware. While the Virginia State Corporation Commission (“VSCC”) is currently

the RERRA for ODEC’s member distribution cooperatives in Virginia, the individual member

distribution cooperatives are the RERRA in Maryland and Delaware. It is unclear whether PJM

intends that ODEC, as the Eligible Customer for Co-Located Loads located in its members’ service

territories, would need to provide certification that the member has authorized ODEC to provide

energy to the Co-Located Load. Alternatively, where the state regulatory agency is the RERRA,

ODEC is unaware of a procedure whereby it would obtain authorization from the VSCC in order

to provide energy to Co-Located Loads. ODEC requests that PJM provide clarification on this

proposed requirement, as it would apply to a generation and transmission electric cooperative like

ODEC.



9
    PJM, Intra-PJM Tariffs, OATT, § I.1 Definitions – R-S.

        B. The Indicated TOs’ Proposed Rates for Firm and Non-Firm Contract Demand

           Transmission Services

       With respect to Indicated TOs’ proposed rates for the new transmission services ordered

by the Commission, ODEC generally agrees with the Indicated TOs’ proposed rate design as well

as the terms and conditions for each service. More specifically, ODEC agrees that it is reasonable

to charge the same rate for Firm Contract Demand Service and NITS, as well as the Indicated TOs’

proposal to use the same Firm Contract Demand Service rate for purposes of establishing the

maximum rate for Non-Firm Contract Demand Service. ODEC also agrees that it is reasonable for

PJM to charge Firm Contract Demand Service customers and Non-Firm Contract Demand Service

customers for applicable PJM administrative charges consistent with PJM’s charges to existing

transmission customers.

       One component of the Indicated TOs’ Initial Brief that may require further compliance

filings is the issue of bill credits for NITS and Firm Contract Demand Service customers. ODEC

supports the Indicated TOs’ expectation that PJM will provide bill credits to NITS and Firm

Contract Demand Service customers directly in their monthly invoices, to reflect credits for

revenues associated with the new Grid Reliance Charge as well as revenues for Non-Firm Contract

Demand Service.10 In addition to its status as a Transmission Owner, ODEC is a transmission

customer under the PJM OATT, as ODEC takes NITS service and pays the NITS rates for several

Transmission Owners in order to meet ODEC’s obligations to provide service to its eleven member

distribution cooperatives.11 It is important that the Commission have assurance from PJM that it

TOs: Virginia Electric and Power Company d/b/a Dominion Energy Virginia; American Electric Power

 will provide the bill credits as envisioned by the Indicated TOs, so that ODEC and other NITS

customers are not subject to paying duplicative charges for the same revenue requirement amount.

The assurance from PJM is also important because the Indicated TOs’ statement that load-serving

entities will perform their current roles of submitting the metrics that PJM uses to calculate

transmission, capacity, and energy charges that as a transmission customer taking NITS service,

may not be consistent among the Indicated TOs. For example, although ODEC is a load-serving

entity, as a transmission customer ODEC does not submit metrics to PJM for calculation of

ODEC’s charges for transmission, capacity, and energy. Instead, those metrics are provided to

PJM by the Transmission Owner(s) for the zones where ODEC takes transmission service.12

Further, ODEC is a customer of AEP affiliate Appalachian Power Company (“APCo”) under a

full-requirements agreement dated August 1, 2017. Such stated rate agreements should ensure that

customers such as ODEC receive credits for revenues received by APCo for the Grid Reliance

Charge and Non-Firm Contract Demand transmission service, so that ODEC is not paying costs

that are already recovered by APCo through these new charges. In order to ensure that rates for

the new Firm Contract Demand Service are just and reasonable, the individual TOs will need to

either confirm that their formula or stated rates and metrics reporting enable direct crediting by

PJM, or provide whatever revisions are necessary in order to do so. Therefore, ODEC requests that

the Commission’s order on the Indicated TOs’ filing require such further compliance filings.

       Questions 3 and 4:

       (3) As noted above, a Co-Location Arrangement is synchronized to the transmission
           system.13 Should the rate paid by an Eligible Customer on behalf of a Co-Located

             Load taking only the new Non-Firm Contract Demand transmission service that
            elects to not reserve any amount of that service for a period of time (e.g., one
            month) reflect not only charges for regulation and black start services, but also an
            additional charge given that regulation and black start services could not be
            provided without the transmission system? If so, how should that additional
            charge be determined?

        (4) As noted above, a Co-Location Arrangement is synchronized to the transmission
            system.14 Should the rate paid by an Eligible Customer on behalf of a Co-Located
            Load taking only a de minimis amount of the new Firm or Non-Firm Contract
            Demand transmission services reflect not only (i) charges for regulation and black
            start service and (ii) the transmission service charges for that de minimis amount
            of service, but also an additional charge reflecting that the Co-Location
            Arrangement is physically connected and synchronized to the PJM transmission
            system? If so, how should that additional charge be determined?

        ODEC supports the Indicated TOs’ proposal for a Grid Reliance Charge to be applied to

customers taking Firm Contract Demand Service and Non-Firm Contract Demand Service.15 As

described by the Indicated TOs, the Grid Reliance Charge appropriately reflects the fact that Co-

Located Load are synchronized with the transmission grid and rely on the transmission grid.

Consistent with the Commission’s determination that transmission customers should be protected

against cost-shifts under the new transmission service framework for Co-Located Loads, the Grid

Reliance Charge ensures that Co-Located Loads pay their “fair share” of costs that are

commensurate with the benefits Co-Located Loads receive from the transmission system including

the costs associated with delivery of black start and regulation services.16

        In its Initial Brief, PJM did not address these questions but indicated that it may provide

additional perspectives in its reply brief, based on review of the PJM Transmission Owners’

brief.17 ODEC believes that in addition to the rates for the cost of regulation and black start

services, the charges for individual Co-Located Loads will need to be determined on some basis

 of the Eligible Customer’s actual or proxy usage on behalf of Co-Located Loads. ODEC expects

that in order to assess charges for black start and regulation service, there must be individual meters

on the Co-Located Loads. PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners will need to address how to

charge regulation and black start service to an Eligible Customer taking service on behalf of Co-

Located Load.

           Questions 5 and 6:

           (5) What is the appropriate remedy or other remedial action that PJM should take to
               address unreserved use of the PJM transmission system for an Eligible Customer
               taking Firm Contract Demand transmission service on behalf of a Co-Located
               Load? What is the appropriate penalty charge or other remedial action that PJM
               should take to address any unreserved use of the PJM transmission system for an
               Eligible Customer taking Non-Firm Contract Demand transmission service on
               behalf of a Co-Located Load?
           (6) What is the appropriate penalty charge or other remedial action that PJM should
               take to address any unreserved use of the PJM transmission system for an Eligible
               Customer taking Non-Firm Contract Demand transmission service on behalf of
               Co-Located Load?

           ODEC agrees with PJM’s proposal for escalating penalties in the form of disqualification

and pauses in service for Eligible Customers failing to shed load or curtail, as well as for failures

in control technology, and/or protection system misoperation.18 ODEC agrees with PJM that

financial penalties alone will be insufficient to address and/or prevent the threats to system

reliability posed by Eligible Customers who fail to control their withdrawals from the transmission

system. ODEC will review the financial penalties being considered by PJM and the Indicated TOs

when they are submitted to the Commission and may offer further comments at that time.

           Additionally, ODEC suggests that the Commission consider whether any protections are

needed for local utilities or TOs should they need to take the extraordinary measure of

disconnecting an Eligible Customer taking service on behalf of Co-Located Loads, if the Eligible

     Id. at 40-50.

 Customer’s use of the transmission system exceeds contract demand or are called upon for Load

Shedding and Curtailment. In such instances, the local utility or TO should not be liable for legal,

financial or other damages that might be experienced by an Eligible Customer.

III.   CONCLUSION

       WHEREFORE, for the foregoing reasons, ODEC requests that the Commission consider

this Reply Brief and condition acceptance of the PJM and Indicated TOs’ proposals for

transmission service to Co-Located Loads on further compliance filings as necessary to address

the following (1) clarification of PJM’s proposed requirement that an Eligible Customer must be

designated to take transmission service on behalf of a Co-Located Load and provide PJM with an

authorization from its RERRA; (2) with respect to the PJM TOs’ proposal for PJM to provide

billing credits to reflect revenues associated with the new Grid Reliance Charge as well as revenues

for Non-Firm Contract Demand Service, the individual TOs will need to either confirm that their

formula or stated rates and metrics reporting enable the direct crediting by PJM, or provide

whatever revisions are necessary in order to do so; (3) PJM and the PJM TOs will need to address

how to charge regulation and black start service to an Eligible Customer taking service on behalf

of Co-Located Load; and (4) the Commission consider whether any protections are needed for

local utilities or TOs should they need to take the extraordinary measure of disconnecting an

Eligible Customer taking service on behalf of Co-Located Loads, if the Eligible Customer’s use

of the transmission system exceeds contract demand or are called upon for Load Shedding and

Curtailment.
